content.thinking:
I'm planning the overall structure of the floating island diorama in one pass: a rocky island about 2.4m across with its tip touching the floor at y=0, rising through a main surface, ruins, and trees up to about 2.2m tall, built from plain objects without needing joints.

I'll create a single root joint at the origin so all parts have a parent to attach to, and figure out the painting approach -- using toon-style cel paints for most surfaces, with the waterfall rendered as a thin textured box showing streak artwork on its faces to get a glowing effect without relying on cel shading there.

For the island itself, I'm shaping the rock body with a lathe profile that tapers from a wide top down to a point at the base, giving it a faceted cliff-like silhouette, with a separate grass cap lathe sitting just above the rock surface.

I'm painting the rock with mottled brown-gray tones and cracked edges using the scales system, wrapped through the cel-shading pipeline for lit and shadow variants. To avoid it looking like a plain cone, I'm scattering irregular icosahedron rock chunks around the lower surface and adding small floating rocks beneath the island for extra detail.

Now I'm sketching the island's overall layout from a top-down view: a ruins arch toward the back center, a pool near the front, steps climbing up to a platform, a waterfall spilling off an edge, and trees placed asymmetrically on either side. I'm working out rough coordinates for each element so they fit together naturally across the island's radius.

For the waterfall itself, I want a water channel running from the pool to the island's lip, then falling vertically down the sloped cliff face, with a tilted box following the rock contour and some splash/mist detail at the base to sell the effect.

Since glow isn't available on sweeps, I'm reconsidering the waterfall as a swept shape along the profile with a painted texture instead—using bright cyan streak patterns to fake the look of flowing water rather than relying on actual glow effects.

I'll add glow to the pool and keep the cascade as a painted ribbon, skipping the extra foam textures for simplicity, maybe with a few semi-glowing mist spheres at the base. Now I'm plotting the waterfall's path along the cliff, offsetting points outward from the rock profile at each height to curve naturally down toward the pool edge.

Working through the orientation of the tube sweep, I realize the azimuth angle I picked doesn't line up well with the simple X/Z binormal-normal frame, so I'll simplify by placing the waterfall straight at the front (azimuth 0) with a small x-offset instead, which keeps the geometry aligned with the Z-axis and avoids orientation mismatches.

Now I'm building the ring radius function that computes the cliff's edge position at a given height and x-offset, then defining the water path and a piecewise profile table for the rock lathe shape.

Now I'm scattering icosahedron rock chunks around the mound, excluding the fall-path angle range, varying their scale and rotation, and alternating tan, brown, and gray cel-shaded colors for a stony dirt look. Then I'm sketching the mossy grass cap with a scalloped lathe edge hanging over the lip.

Setting ground level at 1.05, I'm placing a glowing cyan water pool with a stone block rim near the cliff base, adding faint ripple rings, then running a narrow glowing stream from the pool toward the cliff edge.

For the waterfall, I'm sweeping a path of points down the rock face, offsetting z-coordinates outward from the rock radius at each height to keep the water visually separated from the stone surface.

I'm figuring out where the waterfall should visually meet the rock, checking that the radius function doesn't go negative near the base and clamping it so the fall terminates cleanly around y≈0.3, with mist/foam spheres glowing white at the bottom.

Now I'm adding trailing water droplet spheres falling alongside the main waterfall column, confirming the lathe tip stays at y=0 for a flat base so floating rocks never dip below ground. Then I'm moving on to designing the ruins — placing a back arch and a couple of square pillar columns.

Building the arch structure as a sweep of voussoir blocks along a semicircular path, with a box cross-section for depth and thickness, painted in a scaled stone pattern for the cel-shaded look.

For the keystone, I'm adding a glowing cyan rune decal on a plane textured with an SVG motif, matching the Genshin-style glowing emblem aesthetic I want to carry onto the pillars too.

Now I'm placing the side pillars flanking the arch with plinth bases and cap blocks, adding broken wall segments and steps nearby, then adding two freestanding round columns—one broken at the front left with fluted sides and a lathed capital, one tall at the back right—plus a pedestal with a diamond, and finally ascending steps leading up to a platform at the back.

I'm refining the step placement to lead up to the arch's threshold, then scattering flat stone tiles diagonally as a flagstone path toward the pool. I'm also setting up a helper function for creating boxes with position and rotation to simplify building these stone pieces.

For the materials, I'm designing a mottled stone texture using voronoi-style color cells for a cobbled look, and giving the pillars horizontal banding to mimic masonry courses with slightly staggered joints between rows.

Then I want to wrap this in a `stonePaint(seed)` helper that darkens the mortar lines and varies tone per block using a hash of row and column, feeding into the cel-shaded lighting pass. I'm also noting that at the island's scale the mortar lines would render razor-thin, so I need to size the texel density accordingly to keep the joints visible.

I'm bumping paintSize to 2048 and the line width to 0.01 to get roughly 3mm mortar joints at this scale. For the big back-left tree, I'm planning a curved tapered trunk with bark grain, flared roots, branches, and a canopy built from clusters of faceted icosahedron shapes painted with mottled green tones, plus scattered leaf cards across the canopy surface for extra texture detail.

Working out the trunk sweep paths and radius tapers for the big tree, plus branch placement and bark coloring using a fine-grain cel paint pattern.

Then I'm figuring canopy sphere clusters for the big tree, checking overall height against the reference's aspect ratio, and starting the smaller tree on the right side with its own trunk and canopy placement.

Now I'm scattering bush clusters around the island at various ground positions, then planning hanging vine cards along the arch and cliff using wavy leaf shapes framed with an upward lean.

Then grass tuft cards need placement rules on the cap top, rejecting positions near the pool, stream, and steps so they don't overlap those areas. For flowers I'm planning small colored spheres on stems scattered sparsely across the island, maybe two dozen parts total.

I'm merging the white flower spheres into one geometry using mergeGeometries for efficiency, then placing boulders and rubble: a couple large icosahedron boulders on the top, small rotated boxes for rubble near the ruins, plus a handful of tiny floating rocks scattered at specific positions.

For the floating rocks I'm checking each one's distance from the island's center against the island's radius at that height, making sure they sit clear of the rock mass and don't dip below ground level.

I'm also scaling the scattered chunk clusters so they bulge outward along the island's surface without poking below y=0, and considering adding a glowing crystal cluster near the pedestal for an elemental accent.

Then I shift to decoration: a floating glow orb above the pool, gold filigree trim on the pillars and arch keystone, gold inlay on the steps, and a small hanging tassel-bell ornament from the keystone in warm gold tones.

For runes, I'm designing a glowing cyan diamond texture as a flat SVG, applied as a decal plane on pillar faces with emissive glow, keeping colored textures self-contained so the palette stays limited.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for boxes with configurable position, rotation, and color, keeping part counts manageable by merging repeated geometry like rocks, stones, trees, and flowers to stay under the budget, then starting a masonry paint function for stone textures.

Still writing masonry function...

Now I'm thinking through stone masonry variants and defining a lathe-based column generator—setting up the profile outline for a round column shaft with a base, tapered body, and capital, plus a helper function to place columns with adjustable height and a "broken" option.

Then I'm moving to tree canopies: scattering icosahedron clusters with random offsets and sizes around a center point, coloring them with mottled green cel-shading for a sun-lit leafy look.

For foliage detail, I'm designing leaf, grass, and vine card sprites — small SVG textures with vein patterns and blade shapes — then scattering them across the canopy surface using distance-filtered sampling so they don't overlap too densely.

For the rock material, I'm layering noise-based paints into banded strata, combining patches and stripe functions to fake stratified rock coloring, then wrapping it in a cel-shaded pass for a toon look.

For the island underside, I'm adding a handful of hanging root sweeps that dangle down from the rock body in dark bark tones, starting near the surface and tapering as they drop.

I'm also scattering a few glowing cyan octahedral crystals along the lower rock sides, positioning them radially using a helper function that interpolates rock radius by height, plus adding soft white-cyan mist puffs near the waterfall's base to sell the falling water effect.

For the pool, I'm arranging a ring of twelve small stone boxes around its rim, each rotated to face radially inward, but skipping the one segment where the stream exits so the water can flow out naturally, then capping it with a water cylinder sized to fit inside that rim.

I'm adding a few lily pads as flat green cylinders with pink flower accents, and placing a glowing water cylinder for the pool so its top sits just below the rim height.

For the stream itself, I'm sizing a water box that runs from the pool outward toward the waterfall edge, calculating its length and position so it stops right before the grass cap boundary, then positioning the fall's first point just past that edge so the water appears to spill off convincingly.

I'm working out the shape of the waterfall's path by computing the cap radius at each descending height and using that to place a sequence of points so the stream of falling water follows the curve of the hill convincingly as it drops.

Adding ruin pillar geometry...

Now I'm placing the imposts at the pillar tops with gold-edged boxes, adding thin gold bands at the pillar midpoints, and positioning a keystone box at the arch's center crown with a gold rune plate in front. I'm deciding to keep the arch intact rather than breaking it, and moving on to the wall segments next.

For the walls I'm stacking boxes to form left and right sections with partial second courses and coping on top, scattering a few rotated fallen blocks nearby for debris. Then I'm placing freestanding elements: a broken column on the left-front, a taller capital-topped column on the right-back, and working out where to put a pedestal and small tree near the pool so they don't overlap.

Placing the left-side scenery now: a big tree, a broken column, scattered rocks, and bushes positioned around the perimeter. I'm also working out the staircase leading up to the arch, defining each step's depth and height so they stack correctly toward the top.

Checking platform spacing against the pool edge, I'm placing flagstone tiles along the path from the steps down to the pool, adjusting positions so they stay clear of the pool's radius while keeping a natural scattered arrangement.

I'm hanging a small gold lantern from the arch's keystone, suspended by a rod inside the arch's inner radius, with a glowing cyan orb nestled inside the bell for a magical touch, plus a thin gold inlay sweeping along the arch's curve.

Adding gold arc sweeps front and back...

Actually for the arch I should use radial masonry joints rather than horizontal brick lines, since voussoirs follow the curve — computing angle-based segments every 12 degrees with thin joint lines and hashed tone per block works better. I'll also add a simple moss cap function to place thin green boxes on top of walls, and start thinking about adding vine/leaf details referencing a Genshin-style look.

Now I'm setting up the imports carefully, pulling in only the modules actually used — THREE, geometry merging utilities, the builder, frame, rng, arc/catmull path helpers, paint/texture utilities, and toon/glow kits — to avoid unused import errors. I'm also defining base constants like a scale factor and color palette, plus a profile array describing the arch's radius at different height segments for later interpolation.

Writing lathe outline coordinates...

Checking the cap radius tapering near the top looks fine. Now I'm setting up a randomized rock chunk placement loop, scattering them around the circle while skipping a region near the falling rock's azimuth.

I'm bumping the minimum y value to 0.4 to avoid chunks poking below the ground plane, and setting up chunk colors cycling through rock brown, gray, and pale stone by index. I'm also adding small flattened green icosahedra as moss caps on top of some chunks for extra detail.

Now I'm sketching out a generic tree-building function that takes position, height, trunk radius, canopy radius, seed, and cluster count, starting with the trunk sweep path and tapering radius profile...

Writing root structures...

Setting up alternating leaf mottle colors for variety, then scattering leaf cards and bush clusters similarly to the canopy. For ground cover I'm looping through tufts and flowers with rejection sampling for placement, merging small sphere geometries for flower heads since they share compatible attributes.

Adding stems and vine frames...

I'm deciding the vine cards should face front/back so they're visible, placing some along the arch at select angles and near the pillars, and figuring vines over the cliff face would work too. Now I'm sketching a simple leaf SVG icon with a curved outline and a central vein stroke.

Still writing SVG code...

Now I need to think through orientation: since the drawing appears upside-down when viewed from downstream, the root edge corresponds to the bottom of my drawing, meaning the stem I drew from top to bottom actually has its root at the bottom edge when hung in place.

For the rune, I'm sketching a cyan diamond shape with concentric layered diamonds and a stroke outline, keeping fills opaque since partial opacity won't read well, with a transparent background so it cuts cleanly against the backing.

Now I'm positioning glowing rune planes on the gold keystone and pillar fronts, sizing them to fit within the keystone's gold band and aligning the facing direction to the z-axis, then adding a similar rune plane to the pedestal's front face with coordinates placed just off the stone surface.

For the hanging lantern, I'm sketching a simple design using a gold cone cap, a cyan glow sphere, and a gold bottom cone instead of a complex lathe profile, then figuring out placement within the arch so it hangs centered inside the gate.

Now I'm placing glowing crystal clusters near the pedestal, using scaled octahedron shapes grouped in threes to give them a faceted gem look.

Adding lily pads with small flowers floating on the pool surface, plus scattered stone rubble near the arch and a thin gold trim cap on the pedestal. Now I'm writing a masonry helper function that generates randomized stone block textures with mortar lines for the boxes.

Still writing paint logic...

Writing cap paint logic...

Now I'm working out tuft placement with rejection sampling, generating random angles and distances within the island radius while excluding the pond area and the stream band.

Expanding the exclusion zones to also cover the ruin platform, steps, and arch area so tufts don't spawn under structures, then wiring up frame orientation for each tuft. Next I'm moving on to building the canopy leaf scatter parameters.

Setting leaf card sizes, lean angles, and varied flow directions for the big tree, then picking scatter counts for trees versus bushes. Now writing the cluster helper function that generates colored foliage parts around a center point using seeded randomness...

I'm using faceted icosahedron geometry with flat shading for a cel-shaded faceted look, then working through the tree proportions to figure out trunk height and canopy top position so the overall shape stays balanced.

Still writing tree geometry...
